screening_reasoning: Paper examines word associations in generative models for Slovene language from a cognitive linguistics perspective. It does not propose, implement, or evaluate a computational tool for academic literature discovery, screening, extraction, or evidence synthesis. It is a general NLP/linguistics study, not a research harness for scholarly workflows.

Paper introduces QualiSpeech dataset for speech quality assessment with natural language descriptions. It is a dataset/benchmark paper for audio LLMs, not a computational tool or harness for academic literature review workflows. No provenance, citation verification, or scholarly workflow orchestration mechanisms.

Paper proposes LLM-assisted carbon-aware EV charging framework for power systems. This is a domain-specific application of LLMs to energy/transportation, not a research harness for academic literature workflows. No scholarly discovery, screening, or synthesis mechanisms.

Paper introduces SGR, a stepwise reasoning framework using external subgraph generation for general LLM reasoning tasks. While it uses structured knowledge for reasoning, it is not specifically designed for academic literature workflows, citation verification, or scholarly evidence synthesis.

Paper examines LLM-based agents for autonomous chemistry/materials research (self-driving laboratories). It proposes a five-module framework (Comprehension, Design, Execution, Analysis, Optimization) for agent-enabled SDLs, discusses representative systems (Coscientist, ChemCrow, LLM-RDF, AI-Chemist) as milestones, and introduces the HYDRA framework for benchmarking trustworthy agent-enabled workflows with emphasis on safety, reproducibility, and auditability. This directly addresses computational tools for scientific research workflows (INC-01), incorporates LLM agents (INC-02), describes trustworthiness/auditability mechanisms (INC-03), and provides a benchmarking framework (INC-04). Relevant to all three RQs.
